messages:
Priya (design): Quick design review — interactive legend filtering + keyboard focus order. Posted screenshot and staging link: https://staging.redwood.design/legend-filter-ux . Main issues I noticed: - Tab lands on legend item but there's no visible focus ring (we removed outline earlier). - Toggling a series removes its DOM node which triggers chart reflow and moves focus to a different item (bad for keyboard). - Screen reader reads "button" but not the series state (hidden/visible). Questions: prefer persistent DOM vs virtualized items? What's minimal ARIA we should add? Also copy: should we say "hide" or "remove from view"? Sam (eng-ui): Agree — we removed the default outline to keep things tidy, but accessibility > aesthetics here. I'll restore a clear focus style for legend items (thin 2px ring, using system-focus color). Plan: add .legend-item:focus { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } and ensure keyboard activation uses Space/Enter. I'll also add role="button" and aria-pressed toggling. Ava (a11y): Good start. A few specifics: - Use aria-pressed to convey state, but also provide an explicit aria-label that includes series name + state, e.g. aria-label="Toggle "CPU usage", currently hidden". - On state change, announce with an aria-live="polite" region: "CPU usage series hidden". - Avoid moving keyboard focus after toggle. Instead keep focus on the toggled legend item. Removing the DOM node is the issue; prefer keeping the DOM node but visually hide (opacity: .2 / aria-hidden on series content). - Color contrast: ensure focus ring contrast >= 4.5:1 against background. Luca (pm): Copy note: prefer "Hide series" as user-facing action language vs "remove from view" — shorter and consistent with other UIs (Export -> "Hide" used elsewhere). For the persisted badge idea: when multiple series are hidden show a compact pill: "3 hidden" that is interactive (Enter toggles show all). Also: consider showing a tiny keyboard hint on hover "Space to toggle, Cmd/Ctrl+click multi-select". Priya (design): Nice. Additional UX nit: when multiple toggles happen, chart height shifts a lot. Suggest animate height and content, but keep legend DOM nodes stable. Proposal: fade out series lines (opacity) and set pointer-events: none for hidden ones, don't remove nodes. Also add a "hidden count" badge in the legend header with tooltip and keyboard target (tab to badge to reveal options). Mockup attached in staging link. Sam (eng-ui): Implementation plan: - Restore focus ring and aria attributes (PR -> #ui/legend-focus). - Keep legend item DOM nodes persistent; toggle visual state with CSS transitions (opacity + pointer-events). That avoids reflow and retains focus. - Add Ctrl/Cmd+click multi-select behaviour (will treat Cmd on mac). - Add small aria-live region for announcements. Snippet I'll add to PR:```html
``` Ava (a11y): Quick checklist for testing: VoiceOver (Mac) — tab into legend, Space toggles read properly and live region announces. NVDA (Windows) — ensure aria-pressed & aria-label read. TalkBack (Android) if we have mobile charts. Also verify focus order remains logical (legend items sequenced left-to-right then header). If we add badge, it must be reachable by keyboard before the legend items or via a single skip link. DesignBot: Deploy preview built: https://preview.redwood.design/1990012345-legend-filtering ✅ (staging deploy, ephemeral link). Visual shows persistent nodes + focus ring + hidden-count badge. Priya (design): Decisions & action items: - Sam: PR for focus ring, role/button, aria-pressed, aria-label, aria-live; implement persistent DOM + opacity transitions; add Cmd/Ctrl multi-select. ETA: EOD Tue. - Ava: Run SR test matrix (VO, NVDA) on preview and file any a11y bugs. ETA: Wed morning. - Luca: Update i18n keys for copy (use "Hide series" label) and add keyboard hint string. ETA: Wed EOD. - Priya: Update design spec with badge mock + keyboard interactions, attach final visuals to the ticket. Quick followups: Sam — can you also make the focus ring color tokenized (var(--focus)) so we can tweak contrast quickly? Sam (eng-ui): Yep — will use token and add comment in PR about contrast checks. Priya (design): Thanks all — will track in ticket #UX-842. :thumbsup:
